properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued October 8 at 8:48AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
AQAPSR

The Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (ADEQ) has issued an
Ozone High Pollution Advisory for the Phoenix Metro Area today
(Thursday).

This means that forecast weather conditions combined with existing
ozone levels are expected to result in local maximum 8-hour ozone
concentrations that pose a health risk. Adverse health effects
increase as air quality deteriorates.

Ozone is an air contaminant which can cause breathing difficulties
for children, older adults, as well as persons with respiratory
problems. A decrease in physical activity is recommended.

You are urged to car pool, telecommute or use mass transit.
The use of gasoline-powered equipment should be reduced or done late
in the day.

For details on this High Pollution Advisory, visit the ADEQ internet
site at www.azdeq.gov/forecast/phoenix or call 602-771-2300.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
420 PM MST Thu Oct 8 2026

.UPDATE...
Updated Aviation

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Dry conditions along with temperatures around 10 degrees above 
normal will persist through Friday.

- An Extreme Heat Warning remains in effect for portions of 
southeast California and southwest Arizona through Friday as 
temperatures warm to near record levels resulting in areas of major 
HeatRisk.

- An unsettled weather pattern will arrive this weekend as a series 
of weather systems affect the region resulting in cooler 
temperatures, strong winds, and heightened rain chances. 
  
&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Broad ridging remains in place over the Desert SW, while a small 
short wave continues to push through the Four Corners region this 
afternoon. With enough moisture this short wave may provide enough 
extra lift to produce light isolated showers over the White 
Mountains, and can already be seen on satellite beginning to form.
Otherwise, the rest of the region can expect to be under the 
effects of the high pressure overhead, with dry conditions lasting
through at least Friday. 

The aforementioned high pressure over the Desert SW today has H5 
heights ranging between 587-589 dam resulting in highs this 
afternoon between 101F-103F in South-central AZ. Meanwhile, highs in 
SE CA, and along the CO. River Valley will be between 104F-108F. By 
Friday a troughing feature will begin to dive down the Pacific NW 
states. This will help dampen heights aloft over the lower deserts, 
with forecasted H5 heights between 582-858 dam. Afternoon highs will 
be 1-2 degrees cooler Friday, however Moderate to Major HeatRisk 
will persist in the western lower deserts. That said, an Extreme 
Heat Warning remains in effect for Imperial, Lower Colorado River, 
and Gila River Valleys as well as for Yuma today, then restricted to 
Imperial Valley and Yuma area through Friday. 

&&

.LONG TERM /SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/... 
A major pattern shift is still on schedule for the weekend through 
early next week as a troughing pattern will set up across much of 
the western third of the CONUS. A large northern stream trough is 
expected to dive into the Pacific Northwest on Saturday before 
diving into CA by Sunday. In the meantime, a shortwave trough 
sweeping across the eastern Pacific will pick up Tropical Storm 
Rachel with both systems to be steered northeastward out ahead of 
the large west coast trough. The latest track forecast from the 
National Hurricane Center continues to show Rachel tracking into the 
far northern part of the Baja Peninsula late Saturday night before 
accelerating north-northeastward through the Colorado River Valley 
during the day Sunday as a post- tropical storm. South to southwest 
flow aloft out ahead of the Pacific trough and Tropical Storm Rachel 
will advect significant moisture into the Desert Southwest during 
the day on Saturday with both the EPS and GEFS showing PWATs 
exceeding 200-250% of normal by Saturday evening. The increasing 
moisture combined with an upper- level jet streak moving through the 
Great Basin, increasing the upper-level forcing for ascent, will 
cause areas of scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms to break 
out, mainly over central and southern AZ Saturday afternoon/evening. 

As both the Pacific shortwave and the remnants of Rachel move 
through late Saturday night through Sunday, even deeper moisture 
will be pulled into the region and this will likely be the timeframe 
for the best rain chances across the region with NBM PoPs at greater 
than 50-60% area wide. There continues to be quite a bit uncertainty 
with the rainfall amounts as it will be dependent on the eventual 
track of the remnants of Rachel and will likely have to wait for the 
hi-res guidance data to have better confidence on amounts. In 
addition to the rainfall activity, winds will likely be another 
hazard to deal with, especially for areas east of the track of 
Rachel as the guidance is depicting 850 mb winds to exceed 40-50 
kts, which will likely translate to surface wind gusts in excess of 
40 mph. As both the Pacific shortwave and the remnants of Rachel 
lift to the north late Sunday through Monday, subsidence left behind 
will result in decreasing rain chances during this period before 
chances increase once again, mainly for south-central and eastern 
AZ, on Tuesday as the larger west coast trough progresses eastward.

With the troughing pattern expected to take place this weekend 
through early next week along with the increasing cloud cover and 
moisture, temperatures are expected to take a nose dive. Afternoon 
highs across the lower deserts will go from the low to mid 90s on 
Saturday to low 80s on Monday, with many areas Tuesday and Wednesday 
likely topping out in the 70s.

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 2320Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT:
No major weather issues will exist through Friday evening under 
gradually increasing midlevel cloud decks. Highly variable wind 
directions will be common through mid/late evening before reverting 
to an E/SE component. A few late morning gust 15-20kt will be 
possible, but should be spatially and temporally limited. Very low 
confidence exists regarding wind directions Friday afternoon where 
some aerodromes may become variable, and others obtain a light 
southerly cross runway component. Regardless, directions should 
quickly switch back to E/SE Friday early/mid evening.


Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:
No weather issues will exist through Friday evening under clear 
skies. Extended periods of light and variable winds will persist 
with directions generally varying between northerly and westerly.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Dry conditions along well-above normal temperatures will continue 
through Friday as lower desert highs reach into the triple digits. 
Winds today generally be light and diurnally driven before 
increasing Friday and especially by late this weekend. Afternoon 
MinRHs through Friday will range between 15-25% with fair to good 
overnight recoveries (35-60%). By this weekend MinRH's will rapidly 
improve as a much more unsettled weather pattern is expected through 
early next week. During that time a series of weather systems are 
expected to affect the area with much cooler temperatures along with 
increasing moisture and chances for wetting rainfall.
